title: UC6 Runtime Architecture — one episode
question: What runs where, and what crosses the bridge, during one episode?
scope: Stage A (single robot + scripted NPC obstacles). Nothing is implemented yet; every node below is drawn from the document set, not from code.

zones.label: ROS 2 Graph
zones.sublabel: Python only (NFR-01) · Stage A namespace /robot1, TF prefix robot1/ (architecture.md §7)

card.responsibility: Drives the simulated Waffle Pi body in the Unity scene: applies the commanded velocity and publishes the robot's odometry, LIDAR scan and transforms back across the bridge.
card.constraint: NFR-01 — C# in Unity, no C++. ADR-001 — TurtleBot3 Waffle Pi, no arm; its published velocity and footprint limits set the motion-profile baselines (architecture.md §6).

card.responsibility: Unity-driven moving obstacles that cross the robot's path at a fixed interval. Not ROS nodes; they carry no navigation stack of their own.
card.inputs: Unity scene tick; the scenario's scripted crossing interval (S-04)
card.outputs: Physical presence only — LIDAR returns on /scan and, on contact, a CollisionEvent from the robot's collider
card.constraint: FR-17 — Stage A runs exactly one robot with scripted NPC obstacles only. A second/third robot (Stage B/C) is a different actor and is gated (ADR-006).

card.responsibility: On the pickup trigger, re-parents the item GameObject to the robot so it travels with it; on the place trigger, releases (un-parents) it at the drop-off pose.
card.constraint: ADR-001 — there is no arm and no grasping; re-parent is the whole mechanism. FR-08 / FR-11 are ungraded mechanical support, but this integration point must be reliable enough not to mask navigation results (ADR-001 Consequences).

card.responsibility: Runs the per-task FSM: shelf leg → dwell → profile → drop-off leg → dwell → report. (CONTEXT.md §4)
card.inputs: Task (item, shelf slot pose, drop-off pose, category) from /task_manager/get_next_task; NavigateToPose feedback and result; PickupAck / PlaceAck across the bridge
card.outputs: Two /navigate_to_pose goals per episode; /mission/active_category and /motion_profile/set_category; PickupEvent / PlaceEvent across the bridge; /task/next_task_result at episode end
card.constraint: NFR-03 — does not query MySQL; it receives the task through a service call. ADR-002 — the shelf pose is catalog-sourced, never inferred at runtime. On /motion_profile/set_category failure it keeps the most conservative (Fragile) parameters and logs a warning (architecture.md §6).

card.responsibility: The stock Nav2 stack — bt_navigator, planner_server, controller_server, behavior_server/recoveries, global + local costmaps and localisation — executing the navigate_to_pose behaviour tree, planning globally, tracking locally, and running recovery behaviours before any abort.
card.language: Python (Nav2 stock). Configured through layered YAML parameter files only; no Nav2 source is modified.
card.inputs: /navigate_to_pose goals; /scan, /odom, /tf across the bridge; runtime parameter updates from motion_profile_node
card.outputs: /cmd_vel across the bridge; /metrics/replan_event on a re-plan; the local costmap from which clearance is sampled; recovery behaviours (spin, back-up, wait, clear costmap)
card.constraint: PRD NG3 — Nav2 is configured, never rebuilt. ADR-004 — the local planner is DWB or TEB, selected by the S-04 collision-count benchmark, not preference (NFR-02). ADR-003 — exact server names and default parameter file names carry [VERIFY] until the distro is pinned in Phase 0.

card.responsibility: Turns the active category into Nav2 parameter updates. (CONTEXT.md §4)
card.outputs: Parameter updates to controller_server and both costmap inflation layers: max_vel_x, acc_lim_x, inflation_radius — Standard 0.26 / 2.5 / 0.30, Fragile 0.10 / 2.5 / 0.50, Heavy 0.15 / 1.0 / 0.35
card.constraint: NFR-07 — parameters are hot-applicable per task without restarting Nav2 nodes. PRD G4 — this is a mechanism reinforcing obstacle avoidance, never a standalone feature. Fail-safe: on service failure or timeout the parameters stay at the Fragile (most conservative) values and a warning run_event is logged.

card.responsibility: Accumulates in-run events and hands over a run summary at episode end. (CONTEXT.md §4)
card.inputs: /metrics/collision_event (from Unity across the bridge); /metrics/replan_event (from bt_navigator); /metrics/clearance_sample — its own local-costmap-derived sampler at a fixed 2 Hz; the final outcome from mission_orchestrator
card.outputs: One run summary per episode on /task/next_task_result: collisions_count, min_clearance_m, path_length_m, path_length_ratio, time_to_goal_s, replan_count, mean_linear_vel_mps, outcome
card.constraint: NFR-03 — accumulates in memory; performs no database I/O during the run (data-model.md §6 step 2). Clearance is the local-costmap distance from the footprint boundary to the nearest obstacle; minimum clearance is the per-run minimum over those 2 Hz samples.

card.responsibility: The only node that touches MySQL: reads the task in, writes the run out. (CONTEXT.md §4)
card.inputs: Run summary on /task/next_task_result; the next pending task row from MySQL
card.outputs: The dispatched task over /task_manager/get_next_task; one runs row plus its run_events rows, and the tasks.status transition, in a single transaction at episode end
card.constraint: NFR-03 / ADR-005 — exactly one node performs database I/O, with two call sites (episode start, episode end). FR-14 / FR-16 — a MySQL outage never aborts or blocks a run: a read failure falls back to the last-cached task list or a bundled default task; a write failure buffers to local disk and retries at the next episode start.
cites: prd.md FR-01, FR-13, FR-14, FR-16, NFR-03

card.responsibility: Holds the catalog and the evidence: categories, items, shelf_slots, tasks, runs, run_events.
card.language: MySQL via docker-compose; docs/schema.sql mounted into /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/ and applied on first container start; seeded by script.
card.inputs: One end-of-episode transaction from task_manager: UPDATE tasks · INSERT runs · INSERT run_events
card.outputs: The next pending task — SELECT ... FROM tasks WHERE status='pending' ORDER BY priority, created_at LIMIT 1 FOR UPDATE
card.constraint: ADR-005 — MySQL is the course-locked choice, single-writer. FR-14 — an outage at either call site never aborts or blocks the run. shelf_slots poses are catalog-sourced and stand in for perception (ADR-002); occupied_item_id is not updated live during a run.

card.responsibility: Holds the serialised run payload when the end-of-episode transaction fails, so the evidence survives a database outage.
card.language: Written by task_manager (Python) — the same single node that owns database I/O (NFR-03)
card.inputs: The full runs + run_events payload when the single transaction fails
card.outputs: Retried against MySQL at the next episode start, before that episode's own read
card.constraint: FR-16 / FR-14 — the simulation has already ended by the time this path is taken, so it cannot block a run in progress (architecture.md §8: 'Blocks sim run? No'). ADR-005 notes this fallback must itself be tested, since 'the database must never block a run' is only true if it works.

card.note: Transport: Unity-Robotics-Hub ROS-TCP-Connector (Unity, C#) ↔ ros_tcp_endpoint (ROS 2, Python). One TCP connection per robot instance; Stage A has exactly one.
contract: Velocity command — ROS → Unity — geometry_msgs/Twist on /cmd_vel
LIDAR scan — Unity → ROS — sensor_msgs/LaserScan on /scan
Pickup trigger (dwell complete at shelf) — ROS → Unity — warehouse_msgs/PickupEvent (item_id, robot_ns)
Pickup acknowledged (re-parent done) — Unity → ROS — warehouse_msgs/PickupAck (item_id, success)
Place trigger (dwell complete at drop-off) — ROS → Unity — warehouse_msgs/PlaceEvent (item_id, robot_ns)
Place acknowledged (un-parent done) — Unity → ROS — warehouse_msgs/PlaceAck (item_id, success)
Collision notification — Unity → ROS — warehouse_msgs/CollisionEvent (contact_point, other_tag, robot_ns)
card.constraint: A TCP disconnect aborts the in-flight run as outcome=fail and auto-reconnect is attempted before the next episode — the only failure in architecture.md §8 that blocks a run at all. Field-level message definitions are an implementation task; the names above are the contract graders should expect to see referenced. [VERIFY] against the tutorial's actual default topic set before Phase 1. Whether one endpoint can multiplex multiple namespaced robots is unresolved and gated to Stage B (architecture.md §7).

card.note: The motion half of the bridge contract. Nav2 commands velocity; Unity returns the odometry, scan and transforms that both costmaps and localisation consume.

A collision is a Unity collider contact between the robot footprint and any obstacle, wall or other robot, published as CollisionEvent and logged as a collision run_event. It is the primary thing the grade punishes.
Fired after the dwell completes at the shelf pose and again at the drop-off pose. The FSM waits on the Ack before continuing — this is the whole of pickup and release (ADR-001).
Unity physics only. The NPC intrudes on the planned path; the intrusion reaches ROS 2 as LIDAR returns on /scan, which the local costmap turns into a replan (M3).
Re-parenting attaches the item GameObject to the robot body so it moves with it; release is the inverse at drop-off. No grasping and no arm.
A read-only MySQL query wrapped as a service call. This hand-off is where the episode begins.
nav2_msgs/action/NavigateToPose, served by bt_navigator. Exactly two legs per episode: the shelf leg to the item's catalog-sourced slot pose, and the drop-off leg to the task's destination pose.
/mission/active_category (event-driven, per task) plus the /motion_profile/set_category service call. Issued after the re-parent and before the drop-off leg's goal is sent.

Applied to controller_server and to both the global and local inflation layers, kept in sync, before the next goal is sent. Wider inflation and lower speed reduce collision risk — framed strictly as reinforcing avoidance (G4).
Outcome is the terminal result of the episode: success or fail. Not result, not status — status belongs to tasks.
A replan is a global re-plan triggered by dynamic obstacle intrusion — evidence that avoidance is working, not a failure. Clearance samples are derived from the local costmap at a fixed 2 Hz.
Once per episode end. Episode is the thing happening; run is the row it leaves behind.

edges.label: read task in · write run out

card.note: Two call sites only. At episode end, in one transaction: START TRANSACTION; UPDATE tasks SET status=<completed|failed>; INSERT INTO runs; INSERT INTO run_events; COMMIT.

edges.label: on write failure — buffer, retry next episode (FR-16)

card.note: The point of the single-writer design: the database can be down and the run still completes and still leaves evidence.

mainPath.label: task dispatch
mainPath.detail: task_manager reads the next pending task and hands it to mission_orchestrator over /task_manager/get_next_task. The episode begins here.

mainPath.label: shelf leg
mainPath.detail: First /navigate_to_pose goal, to the item's catalog-sourced shelf slot pose. /cmd_vel crosses the bridge; /odom, /scan and /tf come back.

mainPath.label: dwell
mainPath.detail: The configured pause on arriving within pose tolerance. The robot is stationary and the simulation is waiting, deliberately.

mainPath.label: re-parent
mainPath.detail: PickupEvent crosses the bridge; Unity attaches the item GameObject to the robot and returns PickupAck. No arm, no grasp.

mainPath.label: motion profile
mainPath.detail: The item's category is applied as Nav2 parameter updates before the drop-off leg's goal is sent. On failure the parameters stay at Fragile.

mainPath.label: drop-off leg
mainPath.detail: Second /navigate_to_pose goal, to the task's drop-off pose, with the category profile active and the same avoidance requirements as the shelf leg.

mainPath.label: dwell
mainPath.detail: The configured pause at the drop-off pose before release.

mainPath.label: release
mainPath.detail: PlaceEvent crosses the bridge; Unity un-parents the item and returns PlaceAck.

mainPath.label: outcome reported
mainPath.detail: metrics_collector finalises the run summary and hands it to task_manager, which writes the runs row and its run_events in one transaction — or buffers to disk if MySQL is down.
